title: refactor(app-shell,fields,sdui-parser): one authority each for DataSource, DomProps and SchemaNode (objectui#6349, batch 11)
body:
Refs #6349 (batch 11)

Clause-②: yes

Batch 11 of the one-authority burn-down, on the claim `6116845626` (the last dispatchable batch named in release `6116367377`). It covers three `KNOWN_COLLISIONS` rows: `DataSource`, `DomProps` and `SchemaNode`.

All three rows converge here, so the ledger goes from 7 rows to 4. The four left are the ruling-bound rows: the three Filter rows and `CalendarEvent`.
- **`DataSource`** (round 1): one contract, drifted. app-shell re-points at `@object-ui/types`, a package it already depends on.
- **`DomProps`** (round 2): two key sets behind one name. fields' declaration is renamed `FieldDomProps`, and core keeps the general name.
- **`SchemaNode`** (round 2): two faces behind one name. sdui-parser's declaration is renamed `ParsedSchemaNode`, and types keeps the general name.

**Rounds.** In round 1, `DomProps` and `SchemaNode` stopped with measured options, because every legal route renames or retires a name a package root publishes, and the claim reserves that decision for the seat. The seat's claim amendment `6117134284` answered **A on both**, as recommended, and widened the file surface to the files below. Round 2 implements it. The round-1 measurements and options are kept below as the record the amendment cites.

Implemented in session `https://claude.ai/code/session_016djJF12Qt14ejKR5Vjt4sK` (the seat's session; this was a subagent dispatch).

## Row 1, `DataSource`: re-point (round 1)

**The two declarations at base `2498a07`:**
- `packages/app-shell/src/types.ts`: `export interface DataSource {`, no type parameter. Five required doors typed `any` (`find`, `findOne`, `create`, `update`, and `delete` resolving `Promise of void`), an optional `getMetadata`, and an open `[key: string]: any` index signature. JSDoc: "Generic data source interface. Third-party systems can implement this to connect their own backends".
- `packages/types/src/data.ts`: `export interface DataSource` with `T = any`. JSDoc: "The backend-agnostic data contract every adapter implements".

**Members compared** (TypeScript checker over both built declarations): 37 members in the union of the two, and 0 typed identically.
- Shared doors, typed differently: `find`, `findOne`, `create`, `update`, `delete`. app-shell's are `any`-typed. Its `delete` resolves `void` where the authority's resolves `boolean`, and its `update` and `delete` have no `opts` (`ifMatch`).
- Only on app-shell's: `getMetadata?` and the index signature. Nothing in `packages/`, `apps/` or `examples/` calls `getMetadata`.
- Only on types': `getObjectSchema` (required) and 30 optional members.
- Assignable in neither direction:
  - types into app-shell's: TS2322, "The types returned by 'delete(...)' are incompatible".
  - app-shell's into types': TS2741, "Property 'getObjectSchema' is missing".

**Same concept, drifted.** Both JSDocs describe the adapter contract a backend implements. app-shell's is the older, looser spelling of it.

**Dependency edge:** app-shell depends on `@object-ui/types`. types depends on no workspace package. So the dependency-legal direction is app-shell to types.

**Reach and readers:**
- app-shell's: the app-shell entry does not export it (259 names at base; `DataSource` is not one). The module's only two importers, `src/index.ts` and `components/AppShell.tsx`, import `MinimalAppShellProps` alone. So 0 readers, in-repo and in `examples/`.
- types': published at the types root, and imported from `@object-ui/types` by 232 files (7 in `apps/`, 0 in `examples/`, 18 docs).
- `@objectstack/spec` 17.7.0 has 0 hits for the name (control: `FieldSchema`, 18 files).

**Branch:** "same thing drifted ⇒ re-point", and the re-point is dependency-legal. `packages/app-shell/src/types.ts` now re-exports `@object-ui/types`' `DataSource` in place of its own declaration, with a comment in batch 9's style. The ledger row is removed, and an explanatory comment in the earlier batches' style takes its place.
- An alternative would have been deletion, since the module has no importer, and the effect on every reader is the same. The re-export is the form this card's remedy prescribes.

**Published surface:**
- The app-shell entry's name set is unchanged (259 = 259, one TypeScript program over the built entry).
- Built `dist` sha256, base vs head: of 1,062 files, exactly one differs, `dist/types.d.ts`. That is the declaring module, so the gauge moved where it should. Every `.js` file is byte-identical.
- Changeset: `@object-ui/app-shell` `patch`, since the published surface does not move.

## Row 2, `DomProps`: rename to `FieldDomProps` (round 2, amendment `6117134284`, option A)

**The two declarations at base `2498a07`:**
- `packages/core/src/utils/dom-props.ts`: `export type DomProps` with type parameters `P` and `K extends string = SduiDomPassThroughKey`, equal to `Pick` of `P` at `Extract` of `keyof P` and `K`, intersected with the `data-*` and `aria-*` families. Doc: "The subset of `P` a whitelist of `K` forwards".
- `packages/fields/src/widgets/toDomProps.ts`: `export type DomProps` with one type parameter `P`, equal to `CoreDomProps` at `P` and `DomPassThroughKey`. It imports core's as `CoreDomProps`. Doc: "The subset of `P` this helper forwards".

**Members compared** (probe over both built entries, one `P` carrying every candidate key):
- fields' `DomProps` is type-equal to core's `DomProps` at fields' key set `DomPassThroughKey`.
- The same one-argument spelling means two things. core's default key set forwards `role`, and fields' does not. fields' forwards `name` and `disabled`, and core's does not. The differences are exactly those three keys, pinned with an exact-equality check, and the flipped assertion fails with TS2322.
- Both package files say so in prose: "One MECHANISM, two DECLARATIONS". `@object-ui/components` already gives its third specialisation its own name, `FormControlDomProps`.

**Dependency edge:** fields depends on core. core does not depend on fields.

**Reach and readers:**
- core's: published at the core root, and read through it by 3 packages: components (`lib/form-control-dom-props.ts`), fields (`widgets/toDomProps.ts`) and plugin-dashboard (`schemaHostProps.ts`). 0 in `apps/` and 0 in `examples/`.
- fields': published at the fields root by an explicit `export type { DomProps }` beside `toDomProps`. The barrel comment says it is exported so a widget authored outside this repo can reach it, and the fields CHANGELOG documents "its exported `DomProps`".
  - Through the entry: 0 readers in-repo, and 0 in `apps/`, `examples/` and docs.
  - In-package: `widgets/RichTextField.tsx` (one import, one use), plus the return type of fields' own `toDomProps`.
- `@objectstack/spec` 17.7.0: 0 hits.

**Options (round 1; the seat chose A):**
- **A (recommended, chosen): rename fields' declaration to `FieldDomProps`.** It follows the pattern of components' `FormControlDomProps`. The fields root publishes `FieldDomProps` in place of `DomProps`.
  - Expected root name count: 191 = 191.
  - Files: `toDomProps.ts` (the declaration and `toDomProps`' return type), `src/index.tsx` (the barrel line) and `RichTextField.tsx` (one import, one use), plus the ledger row. All three are on the claim's surface (the declaration site, its barrel, and an importer of the renamed site).
  - Measured on a copy of the built entry: an old `import type { DomProps }` fails loudly with TS2724, whose suggestion is the function `toDomProps`. Following that suggestion gives TS2749, the same shape as batch 10's `ThemeProviderProps`. The new name is type-equal to the old one.
  - Changeset: `@object-ui/fields` `minor`, with a breaking note that names the migration. core is untouched.
  - ⚠️ The name sits next to the existing `FieldWidgetDomProps`, which is the contract's DOM block, not this helper's result. If that nearness is unwanted, a longer specific name serves equally. The seat's call.
- **B: stop publishing the name from the fields root.** The declaration stays module-local to `toDomProps.ts`.
  - The root goes from 191 to 190 names. An old import gives TS2724 (measured).
  - The result type of the published `toDomProps` is left with no importable name: fields' key type `DomPassThroughKey` is not exported from the root either. That undoes what the barrel comment says the export is for.
- **C (refused): re-point fields' name at core's.**
  - Measured with the re-export in place: `tsc --noEmit` over fields gives 27 errors. Widgets read `disabled` and `name` off the result, and core's default key set drops both.
  - It would also silently re-mean `DomProps` for an external reader of the fields root (`role` in, `name` and `disabled` out). That is the shape batch 5 refused.
- **D (refused): rename core's.** It is the general mechanism, with 3 package readers. Batch 4's rule keeps the general name on the general authority.

**Recommendation: A, on the four axes.**
- **Real business need:** both are live. core's is read by three packages. fields' is the published result type of fields' published `toDomProps`, exported on purpose for out-of-repo widgets, with 0 in-repo readers through the entry.
- **Long-term fitness:** one name per meaning. It completes the "one mechanism, three declarations" pattern components already follows, with each specialisation under its own name.
- **Keeping AI from writing it wrong:** today `DomProps` of the same `P` gives a different key set depending on the import path (`role` against `name` and `disabled`), which is exactly the auto-import hazard this gate exists for. After A, the bare name means one thing, and an old import fails loudly.
- **Startup scope:** no new capability, and an immediate rename with no alias window.

**What round 2 changed:**
- `widgets/toDomProps.ts`: the declaration is `FieldDomProps`, and `toDomProps` returns it. Its doc comment tells it apart from `FieldWidgetDomProps` in one paragraph (the contract's non-generic DOM block, against the generic result type of `toDomProps`), and says why it is not `DomProps`.
- `src/index.tsx` publishes `FieldDomProps` in place of `DomProps`, and `RichTextField.tsx` (the one in-package reader) imports the new name.
- core is untouched. The two value-level `toDomProps` functions keep their names (outside this gate's type-level bound, per the amendment).
- Built fields entry: 191 names at base and 191 at head. `DomProps` leaves and `FieldDomProps` joins, and nothing else moves.
- Built dist, base against head: of 88 files, only `index.d.ts` and `widgets/toDomProps.d.ts` differ. Every `.js` and `.cjs` file is byte-identical.
- Changeset `.changeset/6349-batch11-fields.md`: `@object-ui/fields` `minor`, with a breaking note. An old import gives TS2724, its "Did you mean" names the `toDomProps` function, and following that gives TS2749.

## Row 3, `SchemaNode`: rename to `ParsedSchemaNode` (round 2, amendment `6117134284`, option A)

**The two declarations at base `2498a07`:**
- `packages/sdui-parser/src/types.ts`: `export type SchemaNode = SchemaElement | string;`, where `SchemaElement` is `type: string`, `children` as an array of `SchemaNode`, and an open `[prop: string]: unknown`. Doc: "A node in the compiled SDUI tree. Mirrors `@object-ui/types` BaseSchema."
- `packages/types/src/base.ts`: `export type SchemaNode = DeclaredNode | string | number | boolean | null | undefined;`. `DeclaredNode` is the closed union discriminated on a literal `type`, with "No arm is open: there is no index signature and no `type: string` arm here" (AGENTS.md #0.1).

**Members compared** (probe over both built entries):
- Assignable in neither direction. types into the parser's: TS2322 (`undefined` and the other primitives). The parser's into types': TS2322 (`SchemaElement` is not any declared arm).
- At the object arm alone, `DeclaredNode` into `SchemaElement` is TS2322 too. types' `children` is one node or a list, with primitives and `null` admitted. The parser's is a list only.
- These are two faces: the closed authoring type, and the parser's open, as-parsed data tree, whose element `type` is any string the manifest admits.

**Dependency edge:** none for published code.
- sdui-parser has no dependencies at all. `@object-ui/types` is a devDependency only ("Isomorphic, zero React").
- types depends on no workspace package.
- Measured with a re-point in place: `pnpm check:phantom-deps` exits 1, `[dev-only-runtime] @object-ui/sdui-parser imports '@object-ui/types'`. sdui-parser's own `tsc --noEmit` gives 46 errors in its sources (43 in `validate.ts`), plus 131 from types' sources, which need DOM library names the isomorphic parser does not load.
- So a move-down is equally illegal: it needs that same new dependency.

**Reach and readers:**
- types': published at the types root. 37 files import it from `@object-ui/types` (29 of them docs), and 7 more through core's re-export (objectui#4580 made types' the one `SchemaNode` for core). 0 in `examples/`.
- The parser's: published at the sdui-parser root through `export * from './types.js'`.
  - Through the entry: 0 readers in-repo. 21 files import `SchemaElement` from it, and none imports `SchemaNode`. 0 in `apps/`, `examples/` and docs.
  - In-package: `parse.ts`, `validate.ts`, `body-dialect.ts` and `types.ts` itself, plus one test (`inline-whitespace.test.tsx`).
- `@objectstack/spec` 17.7.0: 0 hits.

**Options (round 1; the seat chose A):**
- **A (recommended, chosen): rename the parser's declaration to `ParsedSchemaNode`.** `SchemaElement` keeps its name: it does not collide, and 21 files read it.
  - Expected root name count: 41 = 41.
  - Files: `types.ts` (the declaration and the `children` reference), `parse.ts`, `validate.ts` and `body-dialect.ts` (imports and uses), the one test, and the ledger row.
  - Measured on a copy of the built entry: an old import fails loudly with TS2305, and the new name is type-equal to the old one.
  - Changeset: `@object-ui/sdui-parser` `minor`, with a breaking note. types is untouched.
- **B: keep the alias module-local**, so the parser root stops publishing it.
  - The root goes from 41 to 40 names, and an old import gives TS2305 (measured).
  - The type stays reachable only structurally, as the element of `SchemaElement['children']` (measured equal). So the published tree type has no importable name.
- **C (refused): rename types'.** It is the general authoring name that AGENTS.md section 4 teaches and 44 importing files read.
- **D (refused): re-point, or move down to `@object-ui/types`.** It needs a runtime dependency the zero-dependency parser does not have (measured above). It would also close the parser's open, as-parsed tree onto the closed authoring face.

**Recommendation: A, on the four axes.**
- **Real business need:** the parser's node is live inside the parser, and its exported name has 0 readers through the entry. types' is the authoring face everything reads.
- **Long-term fitness:** two faces get two names, and the zero-dependency, isomorphic parser stays that way. objectui#4580 already ruled types' the one `SchemaNode` for core.
- **Keeping AI from writing it wrong:** an auto-import of the parser's `SchemaNode` today hands an author an open `type: string` node with an index signature, where the authoring face refuses an unknown key. A typo then type-checks. After A there is one `SchemaNode`.
- **Startup scope:** no new capability, and an immediate rename with no alias window.

## Gates

**Round 2, head `69b4a3d`** (base for the comparisons: `2498a07`, whose fields and sdui-parser sources equal round 1's head):
- The one-authority gate: Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 11 passed (11). `KNOWN_COLLISIONS` has 4 rows.
- Through the verify lock: `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/fields...' --filter='@object-ui/sdui-parser...'`, then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/fields type-check` and `pnpm --filter @object-ui/sdui-parser type-check` (each `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, echoed): `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- Readers of the renamed names: a scan of every tracked source and doc file for an import from `@object-ui/fields` or `@object-ui/sdui-parser` finds no code that names `DomProps` or `SchemaNode` (810 files name either package; the only hits are the two changesets' migration lines), and no star re-export of either package. So no dependent reads a moved name. As an extra consumer probe, `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (it imports both packages) exits 0.
- Targeted vitest through the lock: the sdui-parser package plus nine fields suites beside the touched sites (`RichTextField` and the DOM pass-through and leak suites) plus the gate: Test Files 31 passed (31), Tests 629 passed (629).
- A full `turbo run build --filter='./packages/*'` (39 tasks; turbo's build inputs include sdui-parser's sources, so every package rebuilt), then:
  - `pnpm check:readme-exports`: OK, 591 of 591 self-imports judged real, 0 wrong-path, 0 fabricated.
  - `pnpm check:doc-snippets`: 789 of 789 blocks judged, 0 failed.
- core and types: rebuilt with byte-identical dist (216 and 148 files), and entry names 526 = 526 and 709 = 709.
- `pnpm type-check:scripts`: exit 0. `pnpm exec eslint` over the nine touched `.ts`/`.tsx` files: 0 errors (144 warnings, none on a changed line).
- `pnpm check:phantom-deps`, `pnpm check:self-import`, `pnpm check:unreferenced-sources`, `pnpm check:control-bytes` and `pnpm check:test-path-roots`: OK.
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: 0 new citations.
- `pnpm check:changeset-claims` and `pnpm check:pending-changeset-literals`: OK.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: 9 source files of 3 released packages, 3 changesets.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` and `node scripts/check-changeset-fixed.mjs`: OK.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the 13 changed paths: NOT GOVERNED.
- `git merge-tree` against `main` `83b9fad`: clean.

**Round 2 ablation**, through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, with predictions written first. The gate reads source text, so no `dist` sits on its path.
- Control C0: 11 passed.
- S2, the `DomProps` row put back: 1 failed and 10 passed, "DomProps — no longer collides at".
- F2, fields declaring `DomProps` again: 1 failed and 10 passed, "DomProps — a NEW colliding name", naming core's `dom-props.ts` and fields' `toDomProps.ts`.
- S3, the `SchemaNode` row put back: 1 failed and 10 passed, "SchemaNode — no longer collides at".
- F3, sdui-parser declaring `SchemaNode` again: 1 failed and 10 passed, "SchemaNode — a NEW colliding name", naming sdui-parser's `types.ts` and types' `base.ts`.
- Each leg was restored blob-equal to HEAD with an empty `git diff HEAD`, and the tree had 0 status lines afterwards.

**Round 1, head `fb41150`** (the `DataSource` row):
- The gate: 11 passed.
- Through the verify lock: app-shell built (its 28-package closure all cache hits), then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`: `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm check:readme-exports` OK (after building six untouched packages; the first run was PREREQUISITE NOT MET), plus the same check and changeset family as above, all OK.
- Ablation: C0 11 passed; S1, the `DataSource` row put back, red ("no longer collides at"); F1, app-shell declaring an interface `DataSource` again, red ("a NEW colliding name"). Each was restored blob-equal.

Not run locally, and declared for CI: the full app-shell and fields package suites. The change is types and comments only, the emitted JS is identical or differs only in comments, and the suites beside the touched sites ran.

## Acceptance notes (observations, not filed)

- `examples/byo-backend-console/src/mockDataSource.ts` declares a module-local `interface DataSource` (not exported, so not in the gate's population) with a required `getMetadata()` that nothing in the repo calls. It is outside this card. Carrier: none.
- core and fields each publish a function named `toDomProps`. That is a value-name collision, outside this gate's type-level bound, like batch 9's `AppShell` pair and batch 10's `ThemeProvider`. Per the amendment, round 2 renames only the type.
